description: Phase 3 of the 1ppb workplan: atom binding at H_{3A} via the canonical hecke_core._canon chain (convention B, E_0 = Q_β^CODATA). NO FITTING per owner directive 2026-05-10. The residuals vs AME 2020 are the honest exposure of the brane-tower closure problem — the ℏ_q² scaling is structurally correct (via |tr_M| difference); the gap is in the T2/T3 brane-tower terms, not in E_0.

convention_metadata.scaling: ℏ_q^0 (|Δ(net)| = 1 implicit; ℏ_q^2 absorbed into the calibration)
convention_metadata.hecke_level: H_{3A} (atom-level: H_6 D, H_9 T/³He, H_12 ⁴He)
convention_metadata.derivation: Calibration to CAL-3 P_avg^π(n) directly. Sets the operator Δ_NF ≡ 1 in cat-units; canonical for `hecke_core._canon` style chains where the operator difference |tr_M(W_free)| - |tr_M(W_atom)| is dimensionless and carries its own ℏ_q powers.
convention_metadata.operator_class:
Atom-level binding B(Z, N) = E_0 · (|tr_M(W_free)| - |tr_M(W_atom)|) at H_{3A}. The trace-difference operator carries the ℏ_q^2 scaling; E_0 is the unit-action scale.

⚠ CORRECTED 2026-08-31 (bean `qou-zrx2`). MEASURED, the trace-difference operator carries NEITHER an ℏ_q^2 leading term NOR a vanishing classical limit. Swept along q = exp(η) over four decades it is
    tr_M(W_free) − tr_M(W_atom) = c₀(A) + c₁·ℏ_q + O(ℏ_q²)
with c₀(A) = 2^{-A} − 2^{1-2A}, DERIVED (Schur–Weyl at q = 1 gives tr_M = 2^{c(σ)−n}, and the braid words have c_free = 2A, c_atom = A+1 for A = 2..20). So the operator is ℏ_q^0 + ℏ_q^1, not ℏ_q^2. At q₀ the ℏ_q^0 floor is 22.46 % of the deuteron value and 4.88 % of ⁴He's. See computations/probes/classical_floor_derivation_probe.py and QOU/MassTheory/ClassicalTraceFloor.lean (sorry-free).

CONSEQUENCE, and it points the other way from `validity` below: subtract the floor and Δtr − c₀(A) is a pure ℏ_q^1 observable, which pairs with convention **A** (ℏ_q^1) to total ℏ_q^2 — the same bookkeeping as Δ(net) × A, which predicts Q_β to 0.168 %. So on ℏ_q grounds the corrected atom-level observable takes A, not B. Before the subtraction NO convention paired consistently, because the operator's two parts sat at different orders. Recorded as a measured fact; re-designating the canonical convention is an owner decision and is NOT taken here.
convention_metadata.validity:
Phase 3+ Triton / ³He / ⁴He binding MUST use this convention. Naively using convention A with a Δ(net)-style operator difference would miss the 1/ℏ_q^2 factor (≈ 102× error).

⚠ THE ≈102× WARNING CANNOT BE RECOMPUTED AS STATED (2026-08-31, bean `qou-zrx2`). 1/ℏ_q² = 101.862 is arithmetically right, but its premise — that this operator class is ℏ_q^2 — is measured false (see `operator_class`). The mismatch between using A and using B on the SAME trace difference is the scale ratio E_0^A/E_0^B = 5.35, not 102, and two live producers currently differ by exactly that: binding_canonical uses B (deuteron 0.4354 MeV) while derive_binding_chain_cooperative uses A (2.3297 MeV). The 'MUST use B' rule above therefore rests on a wrong index and cannot adjudicate them. Not resolved here — picking the convention that lands closer to AME is the fit this lane has withdrawn three times.
